newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RUTHLESS GULLIT FACES REAL TEST OF TITLE HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUTHLESS GULLIT FACES REAL TEST OF TITLE HOPES.

text.p: Chelsea manager Ruud Gullit, attempting to bring the English League title back to Stamford Bridge for the first time in 42 years, exhibited a ruthlessness this week that has been the hallmark of all the great managers of the past.
Gullit has reinforced his squad this season with the signing of Italians Gianluca Vialli, Roberto di Matteo and Gianfranco Zola.

He recouped some of his 13-million-pound ($21.9 million) outlay by selling last season's top scorer John Spencer to London neighbours Queens Park Rangers for 2.5 million pounds ($4.2 million), letting midfielder Gavin Peacock go to QPR on a month's loan with a view to a permanent 1.6 million pounds ($2.7 million) move and letting out-of-favour striker Mark Stein rejoin his former club Stoke, also initially for a month.

The South African-born, 30-year-old Stein, who cost Chelsea 1.5 million pounds ($2.5 million) when he joined them in October 1993, was the third departure from Stamford Bridge in less than 24 hours and left just one day before league leaders Newcastle United were due to visit in one of Chelsea's most important matches of the season.

Spencer, last season's top scorer with 13 goals and the fans' favourite at the Bridge, Peacock and Stein, had all lost their first team places in Gullit's shake-up but the manager was content to keep them at the club until this week when Spencer criticised him in a newspaper article and Peacock asked for a transfer.
Gullit moved with remarkable speed to release the three, sparking what is likely to be an exodus from the Bridge with David Rocastle, Scott Minto and Frank Sinclair all probably following shortly.
Gullit has also had a row with team captain Dennis Wise and has made it clear he believes that the good of the team comes before the wishes of individuals in his set-up.

On Saturday, Chelsea will have a fair test of just how seriously their championship aspirations should be taken in a sell-out match against the league leaders involving some of the most exciting foreign imports to England.

Zola, Chelsea's new, 4.5 million pounds ($7.6 million) signing, makes his home debut and will be facing his old Parma team mate Faustino Asprilla in the Newcastle side, while Newcastle will also be boosted by the return of England striker Alan Shearer, back after a month out following groin surgery.

Like Gullit, Newcastle boss Kevin Keegan has a popular public persona but has also shown a ruthlessness -- even a stubbornness -- which may not yet have brought any silverware to St James' Park but has helped to transform Newcastle from a lowly team in the old second division to championship challengers and probable UEFA Cup quarter-finalists.

Keegan flew in the face of public opinion when he sold Andy Cole to Manchester United nearly two years ago and has also shown his tough side by keeping former England fullback Warren Barton, whom he bought for a record fee for a defender -- 4.5 million pounds ($7.6 million) -- from Wimbledon, on the sidelines for the best part of eight months following a public spat during a match last season.

Both sides have illuminated the premier league this season with some sparkling attacking soccer, both have frailties at the back and both have beaten champions Manchester United in the last few weeks.

While Chelsea have to go back to 1970 for their last major domestic success and Newcastle to 1955 when they won the F.A. Cup for the fifth time, such are the ambitions of both teams this season that for once the north London derby between Arsenal and Spurs this weekend is matched in both glamour and importance by another game in the capital.
Arsenal cannot be ruled out as title contenders but a win for Chelsea -- and certainly for Newcastle -- would firmly underline their chances. ($ = 0.593 British Pounds)
